findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, a property that has never existed in any IE/Trident release (the real IE10 syntax is `-ms-flex-align`, already emitted on the line above). The bogus declaration is dropped by the CSS parser in every browser, so it is dead weight; a developer reading mixins.scss will assume `-ms-align-items` provides IE coverage when align-items centering silently fails in IE10/11 for users on legacy enterprise builds.

[ADVISORY] The .valign-helper inside .contents is now dead code: its inline-block vertical-centering hack (display:inline-block; height:100%; vertical-align:middle) has no effect once .contents becomes a flex container, because vertical-align is ignored on flex items. The next maintainer changing header vertical alignment will edit the valign-helper and see no effect, wasting debugging time; the now-redundant zero-width helper also renders as an extra (if zero-sized) flex item that participates in layout and order calculations.

[BUG] The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, a property that no browser has ever implemented, while omitting the actual old-Gecko equivalent (-moz-box-align) that the -moz-box display value emitted by the flexbox() mixin would need. Any element styled with display:-moz-box via the flexbox() mixin gets old-spec display without a matching old-spec alignment, so old Firefox renders .contents/.small-action/.badge-wrapper.bullet with default top alignment while every other browser centers; the -ms-align-items line is also dead CSS shipped on every rule that uses the mixin.

[ADVISORY] Converting .contents to a flex container without flex-wrap changes the header's narrow-viewport behavior: floats allowed the .panel to wrap below the .title, but a flex container defaults to nowrap, so on narrow screens the panel cannot drop to the next line and the row overflows. Users on narrow viewports (or with long titles plus a wide panel) get a horizontally clipped or overflowing header instead of the previously wrapped layout; the diff contains no responsive query, flex-wrap declaration, or media-query adjustment anywhere to cover this case.

[ADVISORY] The removal of the .badge-wrapper.bullet margin-top:5px is silently compensated by a line-height:1.5 on .extra-info-wrapper, coupling two unrelated rules across files with no comment recording the dependency. A future edit to extra-info-wrapper's line-height (or removal of it) silently reintroduces the 5px vertical misalignment of bullet category badges that this diff fixed, and the reviewer cannot tell from topic.scss why the bullet override was deleted.

[ADVISORY] Removing the 4em left padding from .small-action-desc changes alignment for small-action blocks that have no topic-avatar sibling (e.g., topic-closed / timed-close messages), where the previous padding created the left inset; the new padding:0 1.5% applies uniformly. Small-action messages without avatars lose their previous left inset and now hug the container edge with a percentage-based padding that scales with viewport width, producing inconsistent message alignment across avatar and non-avatar variants — a visual regression no section of the diff addresses.

[ADVISORY] The .panel repositioning relies on margin-left:auto, but .contents also contains .extra-info-wrapper with order(2) (topic.scss:30) whose default flex-grow is 0, so the free space between .title and .extra-info-wrapper is absorbed before the panel rather than between title and panel, changing which gap visually separates the logo/title from the right-hand controls. Header spacing differs from the intended visual contract whenever extra-info-wrapper is present (topic pages): the title row and category badges group tightly against the right panel's auto margin, and any future insertion of a new flex item into .contents silently changes the gap distribution because no explicit flex-grow/justify-content pinning exists.

[ADVISORY] The PR titled 'Optimize header layout performance' silently rewrites the entire .small-action visual layout (padding 0.5em/4em to 0 1.5%, removal of margin-top, removal of p padding-top, p margin 5px 0 to 0), work not traceable to any header requirement. Anyone browsing a topic's timeline/small-actions (deleted posts, closed notices, custom small-action messages with multi-paragraph p content) sees a changed, cramped layout from a PR that claimed to only touch header performance; a visual regression here ships unannounced and unreviewed.

[ADVISORY] Refactoring .badge-wrapper.bullet from raw properties to mixins in badges.css.scss is out-of-scope churn unrelated to the header stated intent, and the new align-items mixin emits a nonstandard '-ms-align-items' property that no IE version ever supported. The bullet badge's cross-browser baseline alignment is now driven by a shared mixin containing a dead/nonstandard property line; the next person debugging IE-era alignment wastes time on -ms-align-items before discovering it never applied.

[ADVISORY] The .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px } rule is deleted as part of this PR but nothing in the stated header-layout intent requires removing the bullet badge's vertical offset, so the deletion is untraceable scope expansion. Category bullet badges in the extra-info wrapper lose their 5px offset and shift vertically in the header on any topic with a bullet-style category; users see a misaligned badge shipped under a 'performance' PR.

[ADVISORY] The order() mixin emits both 2009-spec (-webkit-box-ordinal-group, -moz-box-ordinal-group) and modern-spec values from the same argument, but the 2009 ordinal-group was 1-based against a different sibling model; more importantly the mixin mixes three incompatible flexbox generations in one rule and @include order(3) on .panel (header.scss line ~36) assumes siblings .title and .extra-info-wrapper have orders, yet .title is never given an order in this diff, making the panel's position depend on default order 0 of an unordered sibling. On any browser honoring the modern order property, .panel (order 3) is pushed after .extra-info-wrapper (order 2) and .title (default 0), but on old-WebKit/Gecko builds honoring box-ordinal-group, an element given ordinal-group 3 with siblings at default ordinal-group 1 reorders differently, so header element order is not the invariant this refactor claims to preserve — legacy browsers render login button and title in a different sequence.

[BUG] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, a property that exists in no browser's flexbox implementation (IE10/11 use `-ms-flex-align`, already emitted on the previous line). The declaration is silently dropped by every CSS parser; any consumer relying on the mixin for old-IE alignment gets the value only via -ms-flex-align, and the next editor copying the mixin pattern will replicate the invented vendor prefix, spreading dead declarations across the codebase.

[ADVISORY] The order mixin maps `order` (0-based, where 0 is the default) to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` (1-based, where 1 is the default and 0 is invalid), so the two engines disagree for any value below 1 and for relative reordering against unset siblings. The current call sites (order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper, order(3) on .panel) happen to stay consistent because unset old-spec siblings default to 1, but any future caller using order(0) or order(1) to move an element before its siblings works in modern browsers and is a no-op or invalid value in the old-box engines the mixin exists to serve — a silent layout divergence on legacy WebKit/Firefox.

[ADVISORY] Converting `.contents` to a flex container while removing the floats makes every child of `.contents` (not just `.title`, `.extra-info-wrapper`, and `.panel`) a block-level flex item, and only two of them get explicit `order` values, so any child without an order (e.g. the sign-up/login buttons styled at lines 34-40, or any plugin/theme injected header element) drops to default order 0 and renders before the ordered items regardless of DOM position. Theme/plugin components and the existing `.login-button`/`.sign-up-button` rules that were authored against float-based layout get re-flowed: buttons lose their inline-block flow and appear first in the row (order 0 vs order 2/3), shifting the header's right-aligned action area on any site with a customized header.

[ADVISORY] `.small-action-desc` padding changes from a fixed avatar-offset (`0.5em 0 0.5em 4em`) to `0 1.5%`, tying the description's inset to the container width instead of the sibling avatar's width. On narrow/mobile viewports 1.5% of the row width is a few pixels, so the description text sits nearly flush against the avatar edge (or at the row start for small-actions rendered without a topic-avatar), losing the reserved gutter the old 4em guaranteed; any third-party style or post type that renders `.small-action` without the flex-ified avatar markup inherits the new tight padding.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes `margin-top: 5px` from `.badge-wrapper.bullet` while making the parent a flex-ordered line box, changing the bullet badge's vertical offset that existed specifically to optically align the bullet category style with the title text. Sites using the 'bullet' category badge style see the badge sit higher relative to the header title line (line-height 1.5) than before, a visual regression on the category header that no flexbox rule in this diff compensates for.

[BUG] The refactor silently deletes the 4em left indent that aligned .small-action-desc text with the avatar column, replacing it with padding: 0 1.5%. Small-action descriptions (closed topic, user warnings, etc.) lose their alignment with the 35px-ish avatar gutter that 4em was tuned to; the text now starts at ~1.5% of container width and visually collides with the avatar — a visual regression shipped inside a PR whose stated intent is only layout-performance optimization, with no design acceptance.

[BUG] The diff removes margin: 5px 0 on .small-action-desc h2 p and collapses spacing to margin: 0, an appearance change unrelated to the flexbox conversion. Paragraph spacing inside small-action headings collapses, changing vertical rhythm of multi-line action text on every topic page — an unrequested visual change smuggled into a performance refactor.

[BUG] The margin-top: 5px compensation for &.bullet inside .extra-info-wrapper is deleted while switching the wrapper to flex order(2), removing the deliberate vertical offset of bullet-style category badges. Bullet category badges in the extra-info strip sit 5px higher than the accepted design specified; any theme or plugin relying on that offset (e.g., aligning the bullet with the title baseline) now renders misaligned.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items and -moz-box-align, properties that are not part of any real flexbox spec: -ms-align-items is a fabricated declaration and -moz-box-align takes different semantics in the 2009 syntax. Browsers falling back to the old -moz-box/-ms-flexbox rendering paths get a no-op or wrongly-interpreted alignment, so the header centering the mixins promise silently fails on those engines — the stated intent 'center-align header items everywhere' is not preserved for exactly the legacy browsers the vendor prefixes exist to serve.

[ADVISORY] Repositioning .panel via margin-left:auto plus order(3) makes the header's visual order depend on flex source order of all .contents children rather than the previous float:left/float:right pairing, changing layout for any child that did not get an explicit order. Plugins and themes that insert additional elements into .contents (search banner, custom header items) previously floated predictably; under the new order-based scheme any inserted item without an order value lands between the title and the panel, shifting the panel from its accepted right-aligned position on those installs.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin passes modern flexbox keyword values (center, baseline) into the legacy 2009 -webkit-box/-ms-flex syntaxes, which only accept start/end/stretch, so the prefixed lines are invalid and dropped by those engines. Users on legacy 2009-flexbox browsers (old iOS Safari / old IE10 via -ms-flex-align quirks) silently lose vertical alignment and get the stretch default in the header and badge layouts this diff converts — a silent partial application of the styling with no error surfaced anywhere.

Only some elements are given explicit `order` values (e.g., `.panel` order(3) and `.extra-info-wrapper` order(2) in another stylesheet), so any other direct children of `.contents` would remain at default `order: 0` and could render before the ordered items even if they appear later in the DOM. The finding’s specific examples (login/sign-up buttons or plugin-injected elements being direct children of `.contents`) are not directly verifiable from this diff, but the underlying risk of unintended reordering for other flex children is grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `.small-action-desc` padding changes from a fixed avatar-offset (`0.5em 0 0.5em 4em`) to `0 1.5%`, tying the description's inset to the container width instead of the sibling avatar's width. On narrow/mobile viewports 1.5% of the row width is a few pixels, so the description text sits nearly flush against the avatar edge (or at the row start for small-actions rendered without a topic-avatar), losing the reserved gutter the old 4em guaranteed; any third-party style or post type that renders `.small-action` without the flex-ified avatar markup inherits the new tight padding.

adjudication.rationale: In `topic-post.scss`, `.small-action-desc` changes from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;` (a fixed left gutter likely reserving space for the adjacent avatar) to `padding: 0 1.5%;` while `.small-action` becomes a flex container. The diff does not add any explicit horizontal gap/margin between `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc`, so on narrow viewports 1.5% can be only a few pixels, plausibly causing the description text to sit much closer to the avatar than before (a visual/layout regression).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff deletes `margin-top: 5px` from `.badge-wrapper.bullet` while making the parent a flex-ordered line box, changing the bullet badge's vertical offset that existed specifically to optically align the bullet category style with the title text. Sites using the 'bullet' category badge style see the badge sit higher relative to the header title line (line-height 1.5) than before, a visual regression on the category header that no flexbox rule in this diff compensates for.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the special-case vertical offset for `.badge-wrapper.bullet` by deleting `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` in `topic.scss`, and it also adds `line-height: 1.5` plus `@include order(2);` to `.extra-info-wrapper`. Those changes can plausibly affect the vertical alignment of the bullet badge style, but the diff does not show the surrounding layout/markup or any compensating rules, so an actual regression cannot be verified solely from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The refactor silently deletes the 4em left indent that aligned .small-action-desc text with the avatar column, replacing it with padding: 0 1.5%. Small-action descriptions (closed topic, user warnings, etc.) lose their alignment with the 35px-ish avatar gutter that 4em was tuned to; the text now starts at ~1.5% of container width and visually collides with the avatar — a visual regression shipped inside a PR whose stated intent is only layout-performance optimization, with no design acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does replace `.small-action-desc` padding from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` (a large left indent) to `padding: 0 1.5%` and removes `margin-top: 5px`, so the finding’s core claim about deleting the 4em indent is verifiable. However, the asserted visual collision/regression with the avatar column can’t be conclusively verified from this diff alone because the overall `.small-action` markup/other CSS that controls avatar sizing/positioning isn’t shown; the new flexbox on `.small-action` may also change alignment behavior in a way that could be intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff removes margin: 5px 0 on .small-action-desc h2 p and collapses spacing to margin: 0, an appearance change unrelated to the flexbox conversion. Paragraph spacing inside small-action headings collapses, changing vertical rhythm of multi-line action text on every topic page — an unrequested visual change smuggled into a performance refactor.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `topic-post.scss` does change `.small-action-desc h2 p` from `margin: 5px 0;` to `margin: 0;`, which will reduce/remove vertical spacing for those paragraphs. However, from the diff alone we can’t verify that this is an actual defect (it may be an intentional layout adjustment as part of the flexbox change), only that it’s a potentially significant visual/rhythm change reviewers may want to question.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The margin-top: 5px compensation for &.bullet inside .extra-info-wrapper is deleted while switching the wrapper to flex order(2), removing the deliberate vertical offset of bullet-style category badges. Bullet category badges in the extra-info strip sit 5px higher than the accepted design specified; any theme or plugin relying on that offset (e.g., aligning the bullet with the title baseline) now renders misaligned.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the specific CSS rule `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` under `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` (in `topic.scss`) while also adding `@include order(2);` and `line-height: 1.5;` to `.extra-info-wrapper`. That is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change to bullet badge vertical positioning. However, the claim that this definitively breaks an “accepted design” or misaligns badges by exactly 5px cannot be verified from the diff alone (no screenshots/spec/tests), so it’s not provably a bug purely from what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items and -moz-box-align, properties that are not part of any real flexbox spec: -ms-align-items is a fabricated declaration and -moz-box-align takes different semantics in the 2009 syntax. Browsers falling back to the old -moz-box/-ms-flexbox rendering paths get a no-op or wrongly-interpreted alignment, so the header centering the mixins promise silently fails on those engines — the stated intent 'center-align header items everywhere' is not preserved for exactly the legacy browsers the vendor prefixes exist to serve.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real flexbox property, and it also omits `-moz-box-align` even though `@mixin flexbox()` sets `display: -moz-box`. That makes the vendor-prefixed legacy fallback path internally inconsistent (old `-moz-box` won’t get an alignment property), so the intended cross-browser centering is questionable. However, the finding’s claim that the mixin emits `-moz-box-align` is incorrect, and whether this causes a user-visible “bug” depends on whether those legacy engines are actually in scope for support.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Repositioning .panel via margin-left:auto plus order(3) makes the header's visual order depend on flex source order of all .contents children rather than the previous float:left/float:right pairing, changing layout for any child that did not get an explicit order. Plugins and themes that insert additional elements into .contents (search banner, custom header items) previously floated predictably; under the new order-based scheme any inserted item without an order value lands between the title and the panel, shifting the panel from its accepted right-aligned position on those installs.

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` was changed to a flex container (`@include flexbox()`), `.title` no longer floats left, and `.panel` no longer floats right; instead it uses `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)`. In a flex layout, any additional `.contents` children without an explicit `order` will default to `order: 0` and therefore be laid out before the `.panel` (order 3), which can place newly inserted elements between the title and the panel—unlike the prior float-based behavior. The diff doesn’t show plugins/themes, but the layout-order sensitivity is a real, diff-grounded compatibility concern rather than a guaranteed defect in core.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The align-items mixin passes modern flexbox keyword values (center, baseline) into the legacy 2009 -webkit-box/-ms-flex syntaxes, which only accept start/end/stretch, so the prefixed lines are invalid and dropped by those engines. Users on legacy 2009-flexbox browsers (old iOS Safari / old IE10 via -ms-flex-align quirks) silently lose vertical alignment and get the stretch default in the header and badge layouts this diff converts — a silent partial application of the styling with no error surfaced anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `align-items($alignment)` mixin that sets `-webkit-box-align`, `-ms-flex-align`, and modern `align-items` to the same keyword (e.g., `center`, `baseline`). The finding claims those keywords are invalid for the legacy syntaxes and would be dropped, but the diff itself shows only standard alignment keywords being used (`center` in `header.scss` / `topic-post.scss`, `baseline` in `badges.css.scss`), and nothing in the diff indicates these values are inherently unsupported by `-webkit-box-align` or `-ms-flex-align`. The assertion about legacy engines silently losing alignment is not verifiable from the diff and appears to rely on an incorrect premise about accepted keyword values.
